Evidence & scope

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv 2305.18290v3) · paper method: DPO fits an implicit reward through a direct policy objective without fitting a separate reward model and running an RL training loop.

candidate.paperfull.dpo.direct-policy-objective

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • The equivalence uses the paper’s KL-constrained objective and preference-model assumptions. Preference-labelled pairs are still required.
  • Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward ModelLocator: PDF p. 4; 4 Direct Preference Optimization, opening paragraph

    without an RL training loop

candidate.paperfull.dpo.reused-human-summary-preferences

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv 2305.18290v3) · paper method: The controlled IMDb sentiment experiment generates preference pairs using a pretrained sentiment classifier.

candidate.paperfull.dpo.synthetic-imdb-preferences

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • These labels are model-generated for a controlled experiment, rather than human preference annotations; the paper calls the classifier the ground-truth reward for this setup.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv 2305.18290v3) · paper method: The paper’s empirical evaluation covers models up to 6 billion parameters.

candidate.paperfull.dpo.tested-model-scale-limit

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • Larger-model scaling, broader distribution shift, reward over-optimization and automated judge prompting are left for further study; no universal PPO-superiority claim follows.
  • Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward ModelLocator: PDF p. 10; 7 Discussion / Limitations & Future Work

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv 2305.18290v3) · human annotation: The GPT-4 summary-judgment validation study recruits 25 volunteer human raters.

candidate.paperfull.dpo.volunteer-human-validation

  • Author-reported, version-specific full-source finding; not independently replicated or approved.
  • Raters are mainly Stanford STEM students/recent graduates/visitors; one late volunteer is excluded from final analysis. This small convenience sample validates selected summary matchups only.
